<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always">&nbsp;</H5><P>
<DIV style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif">




<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt">Exhibit&nbsp;99.1
</DIV>

<DIV align="center">
<TABLE style="font-size: 10pt" cellspacing="0" border="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
<!-- Begin Table Head -->

    <TD align="right" valign="top"><FONT style="font-size:24pt"><I>News Release</I></FONT></TD>
</TR>
<!-- End Table Body -->
</TABLE>

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><DIV style="border-bottom: 1px solid #000000; font-size: 1px">&nbsp;</DIV></DIV>



<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>Air Products and Chemicals, Inc.</B><BR>
7201 Hamilton Boulevard<BR>
Allentown, PA 18195-1501

</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt"><B>HURRICANE KATRINA IMPACTS AIR PRODUCTS&#146;<BR>
HYDROGEN PRODUCTION</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">LEHIGH VALLEY, Pa., August&nbsp;31, 2005 &#150; Air Products (NYSE:APD) today announced that
extensive damage caused by Hurricane Katrina has impacted the company&#146;s industrial
gas complex in New Orleans, La.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Right now, Air Products&#146; primary focus is on the safety and welfare of its employees
in the area. The company will continue to work with local emergency responders as
the impact of Hurricane Katrina is assessed and actions are taken to recover from
it.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Although the full extent of the damage to the New Orleans production facilities is
unknown at this time, the company will be working to bring operations back on line
safely. Restart of the plant will be largely dependent on the availability of
power, utilities, communications, other infrastructure access, and the extent of the
damage.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Based on initial assessments, damage from the hurricane will affect Air Products&#146;
ability to supply customers with hydrogen from the New Orleans plant for an extended
period of time. In addition, the company&#146;s liquid hydrogen production facility at
Sarnia, Canada, Ontario will be experiencing a scheduled shutdown due to a temporary
suspension of its supplier&#146;s feedgas plant. As a result, the company has declared
force majeure for liquid hydrogen at these two industrial gas locations.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In these extraordinary circumstances, Air Products is actively working to assist
customers with their supply needs, including obtaining product from other sources
and geographies. Communications with all customers are underway.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Air Products (NYSE:APD) serves customers in technology, energy, healthcare and
industrial markets worldwide with a unique portfolio of products, services and
solutions, providing atmospheric gases, process and specialty gases, performance
materials and chemical intermediates. Founded in 1940, Air Products has built
leading positions in key growth markets such as semiconductor materials, refinery
hydrogen, home healthcare services, natural gas liquefaction, and advanced coatings
and adhesives. The company is recognized for its innovative culture, operational
excellence and commitment to safety and the environment and is listed in the Dow
Jones Sustainability and FTSE4Good Indices. The company has annual revenues of $7.4
billion, operations in over 30 countries, and nearly 20,000 employees around the
globe. For more information, visit <U>www.airproducts.comm</U>.
</DIV>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt">
